description: Comprehensive understanding of the 12-lead ECG system and lead placement
overview: This module covers the detailed anatomy of the 12-lead ECG system, including limb leads, precordial leads, and their anatomical correlations.
objectives: Identify anatomical views provided by each lead

slides.title: Limb Leads (I, II, III)
slides.content: Limb leads form Einthoven's triangle: Lead I (right arm to left arm), Lead II (right arm to left leg), Lead III (left arm to left leg). These provide frontal plane views of cardiac electrical activity.

slides.title: Augmented Leads (aVR, aVL, aVF)
slides.content: Augmented leads provide additional frontal plane views: aVR (augmented vector right), aVL (augmented vector left), aVF (augmented vector foot). These help in axis determination.

quiz.question: Which lead provides the best view of the inferior wall?
quiz.explanation: Lead II provides the best view of the inferior wall and is commonly used for rhythm monitoring.

slides.title: Precordial Leads (V1-V6)
slides.content: Precordial leads provide horizontal plane views: V1-V2 (septum), V3-V4 (anterior), V5-V6 (lateral). Proper placement is crucial for accurate interpretation.

quiz.question: Which precordial leads best view the anterior wall?
quiz.explanation: V3-V4 provide the best view of the anterior wall of the heart.

slides.title: Lead Misplacement Detection
slides.content: Common misplacements include limb lead reversal, precordial lead displacement. Signs include unusual P wave morphology, unexpected QRS patterns, and axis deviations.

quiz.question: What is the most common limb lead misplacement?
options: Left arm and left leg reversal
Right arm and right leg reversal
quiz.explanation: Right and left arm reversal is the most common limb lead misplacement, causing Lead I inversion.
